name: Hordeum
look_here_first: ONE INSTALLED HORDEUM SPECIES: H. pusillum little barley. See physically archived bristly narrow erect head, NEW credited detached tawny awned spikelet-group close-up, and separate whole stand. On an actual mature attached BARLEY rachis find 3 ONE-FLOWERED spikelets at EACH node: one central usually fertile + two lateral usually reduced/staminate/sterile. That triad identifies the GENUS only. Species split: little barley annual, smaller erect head and relatively short straight glumes; native-at-Texas-state-scale foxtail barley H. jubatum has a much broader commonly nodding fluffy head, glume awns longer and widely splayed, perennial growth. Compare introduced H. murinum's ciliate/expanded glumes and often developed auricles. Wildryes ELYMUS generally have 2 MULTIFLOWERED spikelets/node. Get an attached 10–20× rachis node + mm ruler before claiming final diagnostic proof.

recognition.where_to_look_first: HORDEUM: on the central flowering SPIKE, look at ONE RACHIS NODE for THREE spikelets clustered together (middle usually fertile, two lateral often sterile). That TRIAD means BARLEY GENUS, not LITTLE BARLEY species. Native annual LITTLE BARLEY (*H. pusillum*) has short upright tight spike + relatively short straight glumes; native-to-Texas-at-state-scale FOXTAIL BARLEY (*H. jubatum*, COMPARISON ONLY) has usually perennial base, broad soft often nodding spike and very long outward-splaying glumes. ELYMUS wildryes have usually two MULTI-FLOWERED spikelets at a node.
priority: 1 · TRIAD ANATOMY: expose intact ONE rachis node; middle fertile one-flowered spikelet + two often sterile lateral single-flowered spikelets.
2 · WHOLE SPIKE: little short erect tight 2–9 cm vs foxtail longer (~3–15 cm) often nodding and huge fluffy outspreading bristles.
3 · BARE BRANCH: little's outer glumes ~8–17 mm straighter/ascending; foxtail's glumes ~15–85 mm, strongly divergent bent at maturity, forming plume.
4 · LIFECYCLE: little ANNUAL rooted tuft vs foxtail usually PERENNIAL rooted bunch, stage/grazing complicate.
5 · ELYMUS KEY: wildryes 2 or more MULTI-FLOWERED spikelets per rachis node rather than 3 ONE-FLOWERED barley spikelets.
6 · LEAF COLLAR: little barley lacks auricles; common to foxtail too, so not a standalone split. Need true 1-mm glume and ligule macros.
recognition.warning: Foxtail barley H. jubatum is a comparison-only botanical source, not a new installed species. Do not mark introduced in Texas just because it is weedy; Kew places Texas within its native range, but local county certification is unreviewed. Maturity, drying, and hybrids can alter head appearance.

comparison_lesson.title: Little barley vs foxtail barley — first node, then glumes
comparison_lesson.memory_rule: LITTLE = small upright erect SPIKE + short straight GLUMES + ANNUAL. FOXTAIL = big nodding FEATHER + very long SPLAYED GLUMES + usually PERENNIAL. BOTH have 3 spikelets/node.
quick_split: H. pusillum (only installed species) — short native cool-season annual, compact narrow often erect head 2–9 cm; glumes straight or scarcely divergent, central usually 8–17 mm (including awns) as treated by FNA; one fertile central + two reduced lateral one-flowered spikelets/node.

H. jubatum — foxtail barley COMPARISON ONLY, typically perennial with conspicuously nodding/fluffy flowering head; glumes widely divergent at maturity, typically much longer; state-scale Texas native status does NOT certify Hays.
H. murinum — introduced wall barley COMPARISON ONLY; may make broader fanlike groups, ciliate glumes and prominent auricles; check a mature intact spikelet group and collar, not just head length.
Elymus wildryes — spikes with usually two spikelets at each rachis node; individual spikelets MULTIFLOWERED rather than Hordeum's 3 one-flowered units.
Whole head posture and color vary by age; photograph at maturity and always test a real attached rachis node plus mature glume edges.
comparison_lesson.science_guardrail: No new taxon admitted. Local foxtail nativity not screened; Kew state-level native in Texas. Do not use hairy bristle morphology alone to authorize removal or a plant native county claim.
field_sequence: FIRST: find the annotated SHORT narrow erect SPIKE and relatively close-lying AWNS on the existing little barley photo.

SECOND: in your local rooted plant, isolate ONE central rachis node—Hordeum has THREE grouped spikelets, a fertile middle and smaller lateral companions. This detail is NOT shown in the existing close enough for species-proof arrows.
THIRD: compare the foxtail photo below; mature Hordeum jubatum has MUCH longer glume awns spread broadly outward around a soft, often drooping head.
FOURTH: inspect the whole ROOTED base. H. pusillum is an annual; H. jubatum normally perennial. Photograph mature outer glumes with 1-mm ruler.
FIFTH: before calling it barley rather than wildrye, compare Elymus's MULTIFLORED paired spikelets. If structures cannot be resolved, use Hordeum sp. or Triticeae grass candidate.
photo_targets: Available: existing credited little-barley bristly close head; newly sourced Matt Lavin external CC BY-SA 2.0 detached flowering group macro (provisional), credited whole stand; existing foxtail different-species fluffy head.
TOP remaining: Hays verified attached Hordeum node with THREE one-flowered spikelets, central fertile versus two lateral reduced, real photo 10–20× with mm scale.
Same individual straight central glumes of H. pusillum vs H. jubatum long divergent glumes vs H. murinum margin hairs, measured and annotated only from true pixels.
Expose attached short membranous ligule (~0.2–0.8 mm) and the collar with/without tiny auricles under hand lens.
Whole basal stem and root system proving annual H. pusillum vs established foxtail barley perennial root crown.
Compare two Elymus MULTIFLOWERED spikelets at one rachis node; licensed exact taxon photo, not generic barley illustration.

comparisons.field_cues: LITTLE BARLEY: native North American short-lived cool-season grass with a compact, erect, bristly BARLEY spike. Each rachis node contains THREE closely grouped spikelets (central + two lateral), whose narrow awns form a small bottlebrush. Magnify one node to distinguish introduced foxtail barley or wall barley, and examine the annual rooted crown.
comparisons.lookalikes_and_split: Secale cereale also has a cereal spike but typically bears solitary paired-arranged spikelets (not Hordeum's distinctive triads) at rachis nodes; Hordeum murinum often has broader fanlike awned spikelet groups and is introduced. Cultivated barley Hordeum vulgare is larger and more robust; verify scale and individual spikelet arrangement.

what_to_teach_crew: FIRST: bristly barley-type spike is not automatically little barley; look for triads at the actual rachis NODES.

SECOND: select an ATTACHED NODE and count THREE separate ONE-FLOWERED spikelets, one typically fertile middle and lateral sterile/reduced; a detached cluster photograph cannot reliably orient central/laterals.

THIRD: check small upright dense head and relatively straight central glumes of little barley; foxtail has larger radiating awns and mature nodding head; H. murinum introduced glume/auricle distinctions.
FOURTH: learn difference between Hordeum 3 one-flowered and Elymus 2 multi-flowered spikelets per node, then check the tiny membranous ligule and annual fibrous roots.
FIFTH: image provenance matters: our new detached group is licensed Matt Lavin CC BY-SA from Montana, provisional for user public-page review, NOT a measured Hays microslide.
visual_needs: Highest remaining MICRO gap: one attached 3-spikelet rachis NODE in verified little barley with mm scale, proving real central fertile and two lateral reduced units, not a heap of detached spikelets.

Current new macro is Matt Lavin CC BY-SA 2.0 externally linked detached spikelet groups; review its arrow placement on public learner, and physically archive EXIF-sanitized bytes if adding to canonical media later.
Measure mature nearly straight H. pusillum central glumes (FNA 8–17 mm) alongside foxtail divergent 35–85 mm, with exact local species confirmed and same-scale specimens.
True small attached membranous ligule (FNA ~0.2–0.8 mm) and auricle/collar condition plus rooted short-lived annual plant.
Matched H. murinum introduced glume margins and Elymus two MULTIFLOWERED spikelets per node; don't count other-species photos as installed Hordeum.

visual_comparison.title: Hordeum — little barley live head, shed spikelet groups, and foxtail comparison
visual_comparison.subtitle: 4 source-identified licensed images: the existing local little-barley head, a new CC BY-SA mature detached spikelet group (EXTERNAL, PROVISIONAL USER PHOTO REVIEW), a little-barley field stand, and a clearly identified foxtail barley DIFFERENT SPECIES comparison. Count attached THREE spikelets per node on a future macro before anatomical signoff.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Triad = BARLEY GENUS (one central fertile plus two mostly reduced laterals), not a little-barley species key. LITTLE: upright tight bristly annual and straighter shorter glumes. FOXTAIL: long splayed silky awns and nodding head, perennial. ELYMUS: usually paired MULTIFLOWERED spikelets.
